# Coda API

# Introduction

The Coda API is a RESTful API that lets you programmatically interact with Coda docs:

  * List and search Coda docs

  * Create new docs and copy existing ones

  * Share and publish docs

  * Discover pages, tables, formulas, and controls

  * Read, insert, upsert, update, and delete rows

As we update and release newer versions of the API, we reserve the right to remove older APIs and functionality with a 3-month deprecation notice. We will post about such changes as well as announce new features in the Developers Central section of our Community, and update the API updates doc.

# Getting Started

Our Getting Started Guide helps you learn the basic of working with the API and shows a few ways you can use it. Check it out, and learn how to:

  * Read data from Coda tables and write back to them

  * Build a one-way sync from one Coda doc to another

  * Automate reminders

  * Sync your Google Calendar to Coda
## Free and Paid Workspaces

We make the Coda API available to all of our users free of charge, in both free and paid workspaces. However, API usage is subject to the role of the user associated with the API token in the workspace applicable to each API request. What this means is:

  * For the `#createDoc` endpoint specifically, the owner of the API token must be a Doc Maker (or Admin) in the workspace. If the "Any member can create docs" option in enabled in the workspace settings, they can be an Editor and will get auto-promoted to Doc Maker upon using this endpoint. Lastly, if in addition, the API key owner matches the "Auto-join email domains" setting, they will be auto-added to the workspace and promoted to Doc Maker upon using this endpoint

This behavior applies to the API as well as any integrations that may use it, such as Zapier.

# Sign in and out of Coda

Learn about the various sign-in options for your Coda account, and get answers to common questions.

In order to view most docs - and in order to edit any docs - you’ll need to be logged into a Coda account. If you haven’t created an account yet, follow the prompts to sign up. But if you already have a Coda account, this article will walk through the options for logging into that account. Plus you’ll find lots of great FAQs.

Note that if you’re in an Enterprise workspace, your org admin will be able to limit sign in options. Therefore, you may not see all of the sign in options discussed in this article. To learn more about org admin controls for sign in, check out this article.

# Sign in to Coda

You can proactively log in to Coda by going to coda.io and clicking Sign in in the top-right corner.

Alternatively, you may be logged out and trying to access a doc. In that case, following the link to the doc will lead you first to a sign in prompt.

Depending on your team's settings, you'll be able to log in with any of the following methods:

  * Email and password: the standard sign in option, using your email address and password

  * Google account: use the “sign in with Google” option then choose your Google account

  * Microsoft account: use the “sign in with Microsoft” option then choose your Microsoft account

  * Apple account: use the “sign in with Apple” option then use you Apple ID and password (see FAQs below for more info)

  * Magic link: receive a “magic link” to your email, and use it to sign in without a password

  * Your company's SSO provider: this is only available if you’re in an Enterprise workspace; learn more here

    * Organizations that use Google Workspace to manage identities can use the sign in with Google option above, regardless of their Coda subscription plan.

Once you're signed in, you'll land on your Docs page. You'll see all the docs you have access to listed here, and all the workspaces you are a member of will be listed on the left-hand menu.

# FAQ

Common questions, organized by what you're trying to do.

## Getting started

### Is Coda an upgrade to the Python version installed via Self Service / Company Portal?

No. Coda is a completely new Coding Agent and must be installed separately. See the Installation guide to get started.

### How do I get started as a Glober?

Run:

bash[Button: copy]
    
    `coda --globant
    `

This starts the onboarding flow. Once onboarding is complete, you can simply run `coda` for future sessions.

### How do I check which version I'm running?

bash[Button: copy]
    
    `coda --version
    `

### How do I add or change a provider?

From your terminal (outside a session): `coda --reconfigure`. From inside an active session: `/providers`. Note that `/providers` changes require restarting Coda to take effect.

### Coda opened and immediately asked me to sign in. Is that normal?

Yes. On first launch, with no provider configured, Coda picks the default Glob.AI instance, names it, and asks for its credential: a browser sign-in, or an API key for a key-only instance.

## API Reference

All routes except auth require a `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

### Auth

Method  | Path  | Body  | Description
--- | --- | --- | ---
`POST`  | `/api/auth/register`  | `{ username, email, password }`  | Create account, returns `{ token, user }`
`POST`  | `/api/auth/login`  | `{ email, password }`  | Sign in, returns `{ token, user }`
`GET`  | `/api/auth/me`  | —  | Returns current user

### Rooms

Method  | Path  | Description
--- | --- | ---
`GET`  | `/api/rooms`  | List rooms created by the authenticated user
`POST`  | `/api/rooms`  | Create a room `{ name, language, isPublic }`
`GET`  | `/api/rooms/:id`  | Get room by ID
`PATCH`  | `/api/rooms/:id`  | Update `name` or `language` (owner only)
`DELETE`  | `/api/rooms/:id`  | Delete room (owner only)

### Code Execution

Method  | Path  | Body  | Description
--- | --- | --- | ---
`POST`  | `/api/execute`  | `{ code, language, stdin }`  | Run code; returns `{ stdout, stderr, status, time }`

Locally executed (no API key needed): `javascript`, `python`, `bash`

Via Judge0 (requires `JUDGE0_API_KEY`): `typescript`, `go`, `rust`, `java`, `cpp`, `c`, `csharp`, `sql`

### WebSocket Endpoints

Path  | Auth  | Description
--- | --- | ---
`/ws/:roomId?token=JWT`  | Required  | Yjs CRDT sync for the editor document
`/lobby/:roomId?token=JWT`  | Required  | Room access approval channel
`/terminal?token=JWT`  | Required  | PTY terminal session

# Connecting to Coda

The Coda API uses API key authentication.

## Using API Key Authentication

Your Coda API token (Bearer token) is required to create a connection to Coda. API token can be obtained from your Coda account settings under the API Settings section. Once you have obtained the API token, set it in the ProfileSettings connection property.

### Example Connection string
    
    Profile=C:\profiles\Coda.apip;ProfileSettings='APIKey=your_api_token;'AuthScheme=APIKey;
    

## Usage Examples

AclMetadata:
    
    SELECT * FROM AclMetadata WHERE DocId='doc123'
    

AclPermissions:
    
    SELECT * FROM AclPermissions WHERE DocId='doc123'
    
    
    INSERT INTO AclPermissions (DocId, Access, Principal) VALUES ('AbCDeFGH', 'editor', '{"type":"user","email":"[email protected]"}')
    
    
    DELETE FROM AclPermissions WHERE Id='perm-abcdefgh' AND DocId='AbCDeFGH'

AclSettings:
    
    SELECT * FROM AclSettings WHERE DocId='doc123'
    
    
    UPDATE AclSettings SET EditorsCanChangePermissions=true, IsCopyingAllowed=true WHERE DocId='AbCDeFGH'

# Troubleshooting

Common errors and how to fix them.

## Installation

### Windows — "coda: The term 'coda' is not recognized..."

This is expected right after a fresh install. PowerShell hasn't picked up the updated `PATH` yet. Close and reopen your terminal (or open a new tab) and try again.

### macOS / Linux — "coda: command not found"

Your shell may not have reloaded the updated `PATH` yet. Open a new terminal window, or reload your shell configuration:
    
    `# zsh (default on macOS)
    source ~/.zshrc
    
    # bash
    source ~/.bashrc`

Then try running `coda` again.

## Authentication

### "No organizations available. Contact your administrator."

This message appears during OAuth login and usually means one of two things:

You're using an API key from the "API Keys for Agentic Software Development" email. Those keys are for training/testing purposes only — they aren't associated with an organization or project and don't support OAuth. During onboarding, select:

> Glob.AI OS → Clients → API Key
